summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted following a right ureteroscopy, laser lithotripsy, and double-J stent placement for a 1.3 cm obstructing ureteral stone. He developed rigors and a low-grade fever in the PACU, prompting admission for sepsis workup. He was hydrated with IV fluids and started on empiric antibiotics. Blood and urine cultures showed no growth, white count normalized, and he remained afebrile. His cardiac enzymes were negative, and he tolerated oral intake and ambulation. He was discharged on oral sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim and phenazopyridine, with instructions to follow up for stent removal and INR monitoring. His chronic conditions, including heart failure, diabetes, and anticoagulation, were managed without complication.
